question: What is the characteristic shape of the sigmoid colon?

question: What does the skin usually look like right after a long-term cast is removed?

question: A patient chooses a private hospital over a public teaching hospital to avoid long queues. What does this show?

question: Why are pregnant women and young children most vulnerable to harmful food myths?

question: What is the primary underlying problem in all types of shock?

options.A: Inadequate tissue perfusion
options.B: Elevated blood glucose levels
options.C: Excessive carbon dioxide retention
options.D: Severe localized tissue trauma

explanation: Shock fundamentally happens when blood flow is insufficient to supply oxygen and nutrients to the body's tissues and organs. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h1)

question: When a patient is put on a salt-free diet, what does it mainly cut out?

options.A: Table salt added during cooking or eating
options.B: Proteins found in red meat and poultry
options.C: Every single trace of sodium in fresh fruit
options.D: All water containing natural minerals

explanation: Great job! A salt-free diet simply means cutting out added table salt, not scrubbing away every natural trace of sodium in fresh foods. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h1)

question: Which type of lung cancer is the most commonly diagnosed in clinical practice?

options.A: Bronchial Carcinoid Tumor
options.B: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
options.C: Small Cell Lung Cancer
options.D: Primary Pleural Mesothelioma

explanation: You've got this! Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer accounts for about 85% of all lung cancer cases, making it much more common than the small cell type. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is the main job of a hospital's infection control unit?

options.A: To reduce the risk of spreading infections within the facility
options.B: To handle the daily administrative duties of the pharmacy
options.C: To hire and train new doctors for surgical departments
options.D: To lower the overall cost of running hospital laboratories

explanation: Spot on! The primary focus of infection control is to protect both patients and staff by stopping harmful germs from spreading. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h1)

question: Why does a nurse ask about other body systems when a patient comes in with joint pain?

options.A: It proves that the joint pain is entirely psychological in origin
options.B: Systemic symptoms never occur alongside orthopedic complaints
options.C: It replaces the need to ask about the patient's current medications
options.D: Many musculoskeletal disorders are part of broader systemic or autoimmune diseases

explanation: Great job! Joint pain is often just one piece of a bigger puzzle involving the whole body, like an autoimmune condition. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand how the food supply works?

options.A: Community nutrition depends heavily on food availability and distribution.
options.B: Nurses are directly responsible for inspecting local food processing plants.
options.C: Hospitals must grow their own food to reduce patient feeding costs.
options.D: Clinical nursing duties include setting international agricultural trade policies.

explanation: As a nurse, you care for the whole community. If food isn't available or affordable, patients suffer from malnutrition. Understanding the food chain helps you connect the dots! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T029#GNS227_U2_T029_h1)

question: A community health nurse notices high rates of typhoid in a rural village. Which intervention best addresses the underlying determinant of health?

options.A: Writing a research paper on the biology of the typhoid bacterium
options.B: Partnering with local leaders to build protected boreholes for clean water
options.C: Telling every resident to boil their drinking water for five minutes
options.D: Opening a large tertiary hospital in the nearest capital city

explanation: Addressing the root environmental determinant, such as unsafe water infrastructure, provides a long-term solution to waterborne disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary meaning of women empowerment in a healthcare context?

options.A: Gaining control and the ability to make choices about health and life
options.B: Eliminating the need for medical practitioners in rural villages
options.C: Taking over leadership roles exclusively in hospital management boards
options.D: Ensuring women work exclusively outside the home environment

explanation: Empowerment centers on gaining personal autonomy and the capacity to make vital decisions regarding one's health and well-being. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h1)

question: Which event is classified as an immunization error-related adverse event?

options.A: A child developing a mild fever due to an immune response
options.B: A mild allergic rash caused by an egg protein allergy
options.C: An abscess forming due to unsterile injection techniques
options.D: A baby catching an unrelated malaria infection the next day

explanation: Immunization errors happen due to mistakes in handling, preparation, or administration, such as introducing bacteria through poor aseptic technique. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h7)

question: When does the general survey of a patient actually begin?

options.A: After listening to the patient's heart and lungs
options.B: When the blood pressure cuff is inflated
options.C: When writing the final discharge notes
options.D: The moment the nurse first sees the patient

explanation: The general survey starts immediately through observation before any hands-on examination takes place. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h4)

question: Suddenly, a local government area sees a sharp, unexpected jump in measles cases. How would you classify this?

options.A: An endemic
options.B: A syndrome
options.C: An outbreak
options.D: A pandemic

explanation: Spot on! An outbreak is when we see a sudden, unexpected spike of disease cases in a specific, limited community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T89#GNS214_U1_T89_h1)

question: What happens when a vaccine gets too warm because the cold chain broke?

options.A: It expires in exactly one hour
options.B: It loses its potency permanently
options.C: It turns a bright neon color
options.D: It becomes safe to ingest orally

explanation: Heat damage can't be undone! Once a vaccine gets too warm, it won't protect the patient anymore, which is why keeping things cold is top priority. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h2)

question: Why do we calculate children's drug doses based on their body weight?

options.A: Kids can't swallow adult pills
options.B: Hospital insurance requires it for kids
options.C: Children process and clear drugs differently based on size
options.D: It helps check expiration dates

explanation: Children's bodies and organs are still developing, so weight-based dosing is vital to avoid accidental overdose. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h7)

question: A nurse is interviewing a 15-year-old girl. What is the most important first step to get an honest sexual history?

options.A: Assure the adolescent of strict confidentiality within legal limits
options.B: Involve school teachers in the private interview session
options.C: Limit the conversation strictly to physical vital signs
options.D: Immediately notify the parents of all discussion details

explanation: Brilliant! Teens will only open up about sensitive topics if they trust that their privacy is safe with you. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T5#GNS312_U3_T5_h6)

question: Where does the greatest amount of water and nutrient reabsorption happen in the nephron?

options.A: Distal convoluted tubule
options.B: Collecting duct
options.C: Loop of Henle
options.D: Proximal convoluted tubule

explanation: Brilliant! The proximal convoluted tubule is a real workhorse, taking back most of the good stuff your body needs right after filtration. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h3)

question: What major problem in Nigerian healthcare do HMO payment systems try to solve?

options.A: Too many free drugs in public pharmacies
options.B: Excessive use of traditional herbal medicine
options.C: Heavy reliance on out-of-pocket spending
options.D: A shortage of medical textbooks in universities

explanation: Out-of-pocket spending forces families to pay cash immediately at the hospital, often leading to poverty or delayed care, which HMO prepayment prevents. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h2)

question: Legally speaking, what happens if you perform a nursing care action but forget to write it down?

options.A: The patient must pay a fine for incomplete medical records
options.B: Legally, the care is considered not to have been done
options.C: The physician takes full responsibility for the omitted note
options.D: The hospital automatically waives all liability for the event

explanation: That's right! In a court of law, if it isn't documented, it never happened. Remember: if you did it, chart it! [learn more](GST319_U4_T7#GST319_U4_T7_h5)

question: When moving a heavy medication cart down a hospital hallway, what is the safest technique?

options.A: Pull the cart behind you for better steering
options.B: Hold the cart with only one hand at all times
options.C: Push the cart rather than pulling it
options.D: Run quickly to minimize the duration of the push

explanation: You got it! Pushing lets you use your body weight and strong leg muscles instead of straining your back and shoulders. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: Where do most harmful germs (pathogens) in domestic sewage come from?

options.A: The human gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Atmospheric dust falling into drainage pipes
options.C: Rainwater mixing with soil bacteria outdoors
options.D: Chemical reactions within metal sewer lines

explanation: The disease-causing microorganisms in household sewage mostly come straight from human waste and the gut. That's why keeping waste contained is vital for disease prevention. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the main reason for keeping vaccines in the cold chain?

options.A: To prevent the growth of beneficial bacteria inside vials
options.B: To preserve the chemical potency of the vaccine
options.C: To make the liquid easier to draw into a syringe
options.D: To freeze the vaccine solid before giving it to a child

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines are delicate biological products. The cold chain ensures they don't spoil and lose their disease-fighting power. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T62#GNS214_U1_T62_h7)

question: Which of these is a major use of a PET scan in cancer care (oncology)?

options.A: Staging cancer and checking if it has spread to other parts of the body.
options.B: Measuring the exact physical width and length of a bone fracture.
options.C: Checking the electrical rhythm of the heart during rest and exercise.
options.D: Removing small benign tumors without needing invasive surgery.

explanation: Spot on! Doctors rely heavily on PET scans to see how far cancer has traveled and whether treatments are working to shrink it. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T14#GNS123_U2_T14_h3)

question: What is the main difference between tele-health and tele-medicine?

options.A: Tele-medicine includes nursing care while tele-health does not.
options.B: Tele-health is strictly used for emergency surgical procedures.
options.C: Tele-health covers a broader range of services including education and administration.
options.D: Tele-medicine relies on traditional mail rather than electronic devices.

explanation: Think of tele-health as the big umbrella that covers all health services—like patient education and admin work—while tele-medicine focuses specifically on medical diagnosis and treatment. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the job of beta-lactamase enzymes in bacterial cells?

options.A: By chemically breaking down the antibiotic structure
options.B: By physically blocking the cell wall pores
options.C: By absorbing the drug and storing it safely away
options.D: By tricking the drug into attacking healthy cells instead

explanation: Great job thinking through this! These enzymes act like tiny chemical scissors, cutting up and destroying the antibiotic before it can harm the bacterium. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care for a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: Taking over all daily tasks completely
options.B: Focusing solely on the medical diagnosis
options.C: Promoting independence, dignity, and safety
options.D: Confining the patient to strict bed rest

explanation: Nursing care aims to support the person's remaining abilities while keeping them safe and preserving their personal dignity. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h1)

question: Which of these is a very common nursing diagnosis for a patient struggling with a severe phobia?

options.A: Impaired Gas Exchange
options.B: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.C: Risk for Infection
options.D: Ineffective Coping

explanation: Because phobias rely heavily on avoidance rather than healthy problem-solving, 'Ineffective Coping' fits right in your care plan. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which type of medical mistake happens most often in hospitals?

options.A: Anesthesia overdoses
options.B: Wrong-site surgeries
options.C: Retained surgical instruments
options.D: Medication errors

explanation: Right! Giving the wrong drug, dose, or time is sadly the most common safety hiccup in healthcare. It's why we always double-check our rights of medication! [learn more](GST319_U5_T1#GST319_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which part of a smart bed helps keep track of a patient's weight?

options.A: Mechanical positioning actuators
options.B: Exit detection infrared sensors
options.C: Pressure-mapping mattress overlays
options.D: Load cells and built-in scales

explanation: Load cells are clever little sensors built right into the bed frame that accurately measure weight changes over time. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which hormone directly stimulates the respiratory center to increase ventilation during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: Progesterone acts directly on the brain's respiratory center, increasing the sensitivity to carbon dioxide and prompting deeper, more frequent breathing. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h2)

question: What do we call it when the bladder bulges into the front wall of the vagina because of weak support?

options.A: Rectocele
options.B: Cystocele
options.C: Urethrocele
options.D: Enterocele

explanation: You're doing great! A cysto-cele happens when the tissue between the bladder and vagina stretches, letting the bladder push forward. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h6)

question: What ethical balance must nurses maintain while collecting data during a disaster?

options.A: Balancing hospital profits with the cost of medical textbooks
options.B: Balancing nursing working hours with physician holiday schedules
options.C: Balancing public health surveillance needs with patient privacy and confidentiality
options.D: Balancing local laws with international travel restrictions

explanation: Nurses must track outbreaks to protect the public while still respecting each patient's right to private medical information. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is a key role of the community nurse when a family needs financial or social help?

options.A: Connecting and referring them to available local support systems
options.B: Taking legal custody of their children
options.C: Paying their debts using your own clinic allowance
options.D: Telling them to stay away from government welfare programs

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you act as a bridge by linking families to community groups, NGOs, and welfare programs that can help them. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h7)

question: Why do midwives and doctors check a baby's fontanelles and sutures during labour?

options.A: To estimate the exact gestational age of the pregnancy
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the foetus before delivery
options.C: To figure out the position and attitude of the baby's head
options.D: To check if the baby's brain is developing normally in utero

explanation: By feeling these soft spots and lines, you can map out which way the baby's head is facing and how well it is flexing to come down. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T11#GNS121_U6_T11_h3)

question: In Herzberg's theory, what happens when a workplace 'hygiene factor' is missing?

options.A: It causes job dissatisfaction
options.B: It encourages nurses to work longer hours
options.C: It has absolutely no effect on staff
options.D: It instantly boosts employee creativity

explanation: Correct! Hygiene factors (like basic pay or a decent work environment) won't necessarily make you jump for joy, but if they are missing, you will definitely be unhappy. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the main goal of using the 'substitution test' during an incident review?

options.A: To find a replacement staff member to cover the nurse's shift
options.B: To calculate the cost of replacing broken hospital equipment
options.C: To see if other reasonable nurses would have acted the same way in that situation
options.D: To test if a new drug can safely replace an older medication

explanation: The substitution test helps managers see if any good nurse would have fallen into the same trap. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h5)

question: You just finished giving an elderly patient a bed bath. How should you dry their skin safely?

options.A: Rub their skin hard to wake up blood flow
options.B: Pat the skin dry gently with a soft towel
options.C: Put thick lotion tightly between their toes
options.D: Use a hair dryer on high heat to dry them quickly

explanation: Spot on! Older skin is quite fragile. Always pat gently with a soft towel instead of scrubbing, which can tear the skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h2)

question: When should you take a patient's baseline vital signs when getting ready to give a blood transfusion?

options.A: Immediately before starting the transfusion
options.B: Only when the patient complains of fever
options.C: Six hours after the transfusion finishes
options.D: The evening before the procedure is scheduled

explanation: Taking vitals right before the infusion gives you a clear starting point so you can easily spot if anything changes later. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which temporary change happens to the maternal brain during pregnancy?

options.A: The permanent destruction of frontal lobe neurons
options.B: An increase in overall brain weight and skull size
options.C: A complete cessation of electrical wave activity
options.D: A temporary reduction in gray matter volume

explanation: Don't worry, moms aren't losing brain power! Gray matter dips slightly as the brain smartly reorganizes its neural networks for parenting. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T6#GNS121_U7_T6_h2)

question: In a mass casualty incident, what does a RED triage tag mean?

options.A: Minor injuries that can wait until the end of the shift
options.B: Immediate life-threatening injuries with a high chance of survival
options.C: Injuries so severe that survival is unlikely
options.D: Deceased patients who need no further attention

explanation: Spot on! Red means urgent. It tells us the patient has a life-threatening problem that we can fix right now to save their life. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the classic description of the walking pattern often seen in late pregnancy?

options.A: A fast shuffling stride
options.B: An unsteady staggering gait
options.C: A stiff-legged military march
options.D: A wide-based waddling gait

explanation: Pregnant women naturally widen their stance and swing their hips slightly more to maintain balance over relaxed joints and a heavy abdomen. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h5)

question: What is the best mindset for a nurse handling conflict within the healthcare team?

options.A: Viewing conflict as a problem to solve together
options.B: Reporting every minor disagreement to the police
options.C: Ignoring the argument until someone else fixes it
options.D: Proving that the other person is completely wrong

explanation: You got it! Tackling disagreements as a team issue rather than a personal fight helps everyone reach a peaceful, patient-centered solution. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h7)

question: You just finished explaining how to mix oral rehydration salts to a father. What is the best next step?

options.A: Send him home immediately to start treatment without checking
options.B: Assume he understood because he nodded his head politely
options.C: Ask the father to demonstrate how he will mix the solution
options.D: Give him a written quiz with difficult multiple-choice questions

explanation: Spot on! Having him show you right away is the best practical way to ensure he really understood and can do it at home. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T10#GNS124_U5_T10_h5)

question: A home health nurse notices an older patient's pension checks are missing and lights are cut off despite having funds. What is going on here?

options.A: Physical neglect
options.B: Active abandonment
options.C: Financial exploitation
options.D: Emotional maltreatment

explanation: Taking or misusing a vulnerable person's money or resources is financial exploitation. You're building great clinical intuition! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T10#GNS324_U3_T10_h2)

question: As a nurse, why do you need to monitor patients with digestive disorders very closely?

options.A: Digestive issues never change after admission
options.B: Intestinal tracts do not connect to other systems
options.C: The gut controls vital fluid and acid-base balance
options.D: Patients with gut problems refuse all medication

explanation: Spot on! The gut manages critical body functions like fluids and chemistry. When things go wrong there, the whole body feels it. You are getting the hang of this! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h1)

question: What is the main job of the tiny bones (ossicles) in the middle ear?

options.A: Equalize air pressure behind the eardrum
options.B: Amplify and transmit sound vibrations to the inner ear
options.C: Produce earwax to protect the ear canal
options.D: Translate electrical signals into spoken words

explanation: These three little bones act like a sound system amplifier. When sound hits your eardrum, they boost the vibration and pass it smoothly into the inner ear fluid. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why do nurses compare data collected after a health campaign with the baseline numbers gathered before it started?

options.A: To satisfy personal curiosity about how many posters were printed
options.B: To determine if the health campaign actually caused positive behavior changes
options.C: To calculate the exact travel expenses of the visiting health team
options.D: To prove that no one in the community attended any health meetings

explanation: Spot on! Comparing 'before' and 'after' numbers is the only way to prove whether your awareness campaign truly made a difference. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign or effect of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)?

options.A: Presence of multiple small ovarian cysts
options.B: Irregular or absent ovulation
options.C: Interference with normal follicular development
options.D: Continuous production of excess mature ova

explanation: PCOS actually makes normal ovulation harder, rather than flooding the body with extra healthy, mature eggs. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h7)

question: A patient with newly diagnosed severe kidney disease needs help managing their protein and potassium intake. Which setting is best?

options.A: Individual counselling
options.B: General television health ads
options.C: Group dietary classes
options.D: A public community workshop

explanation: New, complex diagnoses need one-on-one attention to review lab values and build a safe, highly specific meal plan. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h2)

question: A patient has a pressure sore with a thick layer of black dead tissue covering the base. What action is needed first for effective healing?

options.A: Applying dry gauze directly over the black tissue
options.B: Debridement to remove the dead tissue
options.C: Immediate closure with skin grafts without cleaning
options.D: Soaking the entire wound in hydrogen peroxide daily

explanation: That black dead tissue (eschar) acts like a shield trapping bacteria and blocking new growth. It has to be safely cleared away (debrided) before healing can truly begin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h5)

question: When counseling pregnant women about traditional food habits, which approach is NOT helpful?

options.A: Listening carefully to the patient's family and cultural beliefs
options.B: Incorporating affordable local staples like beans and dark leafy greens
options.C: Identifying harmful taboos without disrespecting the community
options.D: Insisting that only imported foreign foods can provide proper prenatal nutrition

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing care relies on affordable, local foods that everyday families can actually get, not expensive foreign items. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T008#GNS227_U2_T008_h7)

question: A patient with persistent asthma is prescribed a daily inhaler that works for 12 hours. What drug class is this?

options.A: Short-acting anticholinergics
options.B: Short-Acting Beta-Agonists
options.C: Long-Acting Beta-Agonists
options.D: Inhaled corticosteroids

explanation: That's a Long-Acting Beta-Agonist (LABA)! While SABAs are for quick rescue, LABAs provide steady, long-lasting control throughout the day. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the main route of transmission for the pathogens that cause gastroenteritis?

options.A: Fecal-oral route
options.B: Broken skin contact
options.C: Direct droplet inhalation
options.D: Vector-borne mosquito bites

explanation: Gastroenteritis pathogens spread primarily when microscopic amounts of infected stool contaminate food, water, or hands and enter a new host's mouth. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: Why do we apply that slippery water-based gel to a patient's skin before doing an ultrasound?

options.A: To get rid of air pockets that block sound waves
options.B: To cool down the hot scanner probe
options.C: To numb the skin so the scan doesn't hurt
options.D: To leave a mark on the skin for later

explanation: Sound waves struggle to travel through air. The gel acts like a bridge, helping the waves glide smoothly into the body. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h2)

question: What does it mean to write a 'contemporaneous' nursing note?

options.A: It is written using official medical shorthand
options.B: It is written at the end of the entire work week
options.C: It is written close to the time care is given
options.D: It is written by a senior doctor only

explanation: Spot on! Writing notes right away means you don't have to rely on memory, keeping the true timeline safe. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why do many patients having severe anxiety rush to the emergency clinic complaining of chest pain and dizziness?

options.A: Anxiety triggers physical symptoms that mimic serious medical conditions like heart trouble.
options.B: Patients prefer to hide their mental health struggles from healthcare providers.
options.C: Anxiety only affects internal organs and has no psychological components.
options.D: Medical clinics offer free counseling for psychiatric disorders.

explanation: Anxiety doesn't just feel mental—it feels very physical! Racing hearts and chest tightness feel so much like a heart attack that patients naturally seek emergency help first. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which core nursing ethic requires you to keep a survivor's identity and story strictly secret?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Justice
options.C: Veracity
options.D: Confidentiality

explanation: Confidentiality protects patients from stigma and further danger by making sure their private health details never leak out without their consent. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T11#GNS312_U4_T11_h7)

question: In stroke care, what does 'spasticity' mean?

options.A: Rapid wasting away of muscle tissue
options.B: Complete loss of all muscle sensation
options.C: Uncontrolled trembling during resting states
options.D: Involuntary muscle stiffness and tight spasms

explanation: Spot on! Spasticity is when muscles become tight and stiff because of nerve damage, making them hard to stretch out. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T9#GNS324_U4_T9_h4)

question: Why do doctors perform a paracentesis on a patient with heavy fluid buildup in the belly?

options.A: To permanently cure chronic liver failure
options.B: To deliver oral medications directly to the gut
options.C: To remove excess fluid and relieve pressure
options.D: To flush the kidneys with sterile saline

explanation: Draining that trapped fluid makes the patient so much more comfortable and helps them breathe easier. Simple as that! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T19#GNS221_U2_T19_h1)

question: What is the main goal of dietary counselling when you're working with a patient?

options.A: Enforcing hospital cafeteria meal schedules on patients
options.B: Helping individuals make sustainable food choices for health
options.C: Strictly prescribing medications for nutritional deficiencies
options.D: Eliminating all carbohydrates from the patient daily intake

explanation: You're helping patients build lifelong healthy eating habits, not just quick fixes. Great job thinking about long-term wellness! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h1)

question: Why does the PMTCT strategy include primary prevention of HIV in women as its first prong?

options.A: Antiretroviral drugs are too expensive to give to pregnant women.
options.B: Men do not play any role in the transmission of the virus.
options.C: Uninfected women of childbearing age cannot transmit a virus they do not have.
options.D: Primary prevention replaces the need for infant diagnostic testing.

explanation: Stopping women from contracting HIV in the first place eliminates the possibility of vertical transmission entirely. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h3)

question: Why do nurses constantly remind patients receiving radiation therapy not to wash off their skin treatment marks?

options.A: To prevent the patient from developing a severe skin allergy to the ink
options.B: To keep the hospital records accurate for billing and insurance purposes
options.C: To allow the radiation oncologists to track how fast the outer tumor is shrinking
options.D: To ensure precise daily alignment of the radiation beam to the exact tumor site

question: What is the main function of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

question: Which family dynamic is most strongly linked to an increased risk of early unprotected sex in teens?

question: How do researchers know when they have enough participants in a qualitative nursing study?

question: What does a nurse do when acting as a facilitator of health education?

options.C: Performs complex surgical procedures alone
options.D: Guides patients toward healthier choices instead of just lecturing them

question: Which of the following is a key criterion used to prioritize community health problems?

options.B: Magnitude or number of people affected

options.D: The architectural design of the local health clinic

question: How does poor nutrition in a pregnant mother directly affect her unborn baby?

options.A: It prevents the development of neonatal jaundice entirely
options.B: It causes the baby to be born with complete immunity to infections
options.C: It accelerates the closure of the infant's fontanelles

question: Since there is no cure for established paralytic polio, what is the main goal of treatment?

options.A: Immediate surgical repair of damaged motor neurons
options.B: Supportive care and complication prevention
options.C: Direct antiviral elimination of the virus from nerves
options.D: Aggressive immune suppression therapy

question: What happens during passive health surveillance?

options.A: The government bans the collection of all health statistics
options.B: Nurses actively hunt for sick people in every single household
options.C: Patients diagnose themselves at home without telling anyone
options.D: Clinics routinely report disease cases upward to health authorities

explanation: In passive surveillance, we wait for patients to come to the clinic feeling unwell, and then our routine reports flow up to the health authorities. It's the standard way we track everyday illnesses! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h3)

question: Why are informal sector workers in developing regions often at a higher risk for occupational lung disease?

options.A: Government laws completely ban safety masks in local factories
options.B: The tropical climate causes dust particles to become radioactive
options.C: They frequently lack proper personal protective equipment and health monitoring
options.D: Their lungs are naturally weaker than those of corporate office workers

question: Where and when was the global declaration reaffirming primary health care signed to mark the 40th anniversary of Alma-Ata?

question: What is the name of the middle phase of yellow fever when a patient's early symptoms temporarily disappear?

explanation: That's correct! During the remission phase, the patient might feel like they are magically getting better before any severe symptoms hit. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of triage in an emergency department?

options.A: Sorting patients based on injury severity
options.B: Determining the patient's insurance status
options.C: Collecting payment before starting care
options.D: Registering patient names and addresses

explanation: Triage prioritizes care so that patients with the most life-threatening conditions receive immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h1)

question: Which of these conditions is a major reason to put a patient on a low-sodium diet?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia

options.C: Chronic bone fractures
options.D: Congestive heart failure

question: What dangerous hazard is often associated with bulging food cans?

options.A: High vitamin C loss

options.D: Botulinum toxins

explanation: A bulging can indicates gas production by bacteria, most notably the dangerous bacterium that causes botulism. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h4)

question: Why do memory or brain issues usually affect IADLs before basic ADLs?

options.A: Patients always get more help with cooking than bathing.

options.C: Basic ADLs depend entirely on memory, not muscles.
options.D: Brain changes never affect physical self-care.

question: Which life stage is especially known for triggering or worsening domestic violence?

options.A: Adolescence

question: What term describes shaky, clumsy, and uncoordinated muscle movements caused by a problem in the cerebellum?

options.A: Akinetopsia

options.D: Ataxia

question: Why do dialogue groups involving village elders and men help improve women's health access?

options.C: They prevent women from leaving their homes for any reason

question: Whose responsibility is it to ensure visitors follow isolation rules in a patient's room?

options.A: The nurse caring for the patient

options.D: The dietary staff delivering meals

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a health project?

options.C: Monitoring deals only with money, while evaluation deals only with staff

question: What is the main purpose of doing a 'test of change' in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To conduct a massive clinical trial on new surgical equipment
options.B: To try out a new idea on a small scale before full implementation
options.C: To permanently rewrite the national nursing practice guidelines

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication?

question: What is the primary activity that takes place during the implementation phase of the health planning cycle?

question: Where are the developing egg follicles primarily housed within the ovary?

question: How is a nuclear medicine bone scan different from a regular X-ray?

options.A: It uses sound waves to check blood flow inside the bone marrow

question: What is the main goal of hospital antibiotic stewardship programs?

question: What happens if a traction rope slips out of its pulley groove?

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge to collaboration in low-resource settings?

question: How do smart beds help keep vulnerable hospital patients safe?

question: A patient has been convulsing for eight minutes straight without waking up. What is your immediate nursing priority?

question: Which type of FGM involves cutting and repositioning the labia to create a covering seal over the vaginal opening?

question: What is a major risk of pushing a client too early into regular open employment?

question: When teaching a patient about nutrition, which factor must you always keep in mind?

question: Which of these is a major headache for tracking nursing costs in many Nigerian hospitals?

question: What fluid is found mainly inside the inner ear's membranous labyrinth?

question: What is the primary role of calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D produced by the kidneys?

question: A community needs a ward-level facility that can handle 24-hour deliveries and minor procedures. Which one should they use?

question: Why do toddlers often experience a sudden drop in appetite?

question: In secretory diarrhoea, why do patients lose water so quickly?

question: Which type of medication is given to treat intestinal worm infections?

question: Why is modern healthcare now encouraging fathers to get involved during pregnancy?

question: What is gluten's main job when baking bread and pastries?

question: What is the main way chloroquine fights against the malaria parasite?

question: Why is proper ergonomic design particularly important for healthcare professionals?

question: Why are normal losses from breathing and light sweating called insensible fluid losses?

question: What is the main difference between corrective action and preventive action?

question: Why are nurses considered frontline defenders in occupational health?

question: What makes data a 'primary source' in research?

question: How do everyday nursing activities relate to research data?

options.C: Nurses only encounter research data when publishing academic books

question: Why does visiting a patient's home often reveal health details that a clinic visit misses?

question: Why do state or regional health schemes often exist alongside a national scheme?

question: Why is it so important to include frontline nurses when reviewing hospital policies?

options.C: To fulfill a legal requirement that nurses write all hospital laws

question: Which mistake during a cervical swab can ruin the lab result?

question: Why do many patients stop taking their blood pressure medication without telling their nurse?

question: What is the main job of hormones in our bodies?

question: When would a nurse use an oropharyngeal airway device?

question: Which metabolic pathway breaks down large molecules and releases energy?

question: How do private health insurance companies usually decide how much you will pay for your monthly premium?

question: What is the primary function of the microscopic microvilli lining the proximal convoluted tubule?

question: A sudden plant disease wipes out a large portion of local cassava crops. Based on market dynamics, what is the most likely immediate result for consumers?

question: How can a Guinea worm infection lead to permanent joint stiffness?

options.D: Mosquito forceps

question: What happens during the process of opsonization?

options.A: Blood vessels constrict to stop the spread of an infection
options.B: Antibodies punch direct holes in the cell wall of a virus
options.C: Red blood cells are destroyed to release iron to the tissues
options.D: Pathogens are coated with antibodies to help phagocytes swallow them

explanation: Opsonization is basically tagging an enemy for easy spotting. It's like putting a handle on a pathogen so immune cells like macrophages can easily grab and engulf it! [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h4)

question: A nurse researcher discovers new home care tips for elderly patients. Which dissemination strategy reaches the patients and their families best?

options.A: Archiving the raw data files in a secure university computer vault
options.B: Submitting a heavily statistical paper to an advanced physics journal
options.C: Presenting a complex data analysis at a closed medical board meeting
options.D: Creating simple health flyers and speaking at local community centers

explanation: Patients and families respond best to direct, community-level outreach in plain, easy-to-understand language. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h8)

question: What do we call the inner struggle a person feels regarding their beliefs or connection to the sacred?

options.A: Somatic disorder
options.B: Sensory overload
options.C: Cognitive fatigue
options.D: Spiritual distress

explanation: Spiritual distress happens when someone goes through a deep crisis that shakes their faith, beliefs, or sense of purpose. Spotting this helps us support them better. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h3)

question: What is the main drawback of a positive Mantoux (tuberculin skin) test?

options.A: It cannot distinguish between latent and active infection
options.B: It only works in patients who have never received vaccinations
options.C: It is completely unreliable for diagnosing immunocompromised adults
options.D: It requires laboratory analysis of blood within two hours

explanation: A positive skin test simply means your immune system has seen TB before. It cannot tell if the infection is sleeping (latent) or active. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h4)

question: How do safety checklists contribute to quality patient care in clinical practice?

options.A: They shorten the operating time for emergency surgeries
options.B: They automatically record the patient's vital signs into the computer
options.C: They replace the need for professional nursing judgment
options.D: They prevent the omission of critical steps during complex procedures

explanation: Checklists serve as memory aids to ensure that vital safety steps are never skipped during busy or high-stress procedures. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h7)

question: Why is obtaining thorough informed consent especially critical before a patient undergoes presymptomatic genetic testing?

options.A: Insurance companies always pay for the treatment if results are positive
options.B: Genetic tests are legally required for all adult citizens
options.C: The results carry heavy emotional, psychological, and social implications
options.D: The testing procedure itself is physically painful and invasive

explanation: Learning about a future untreatable degenerative condition can profoundly impact a person's mental health, family dynamics, and future planning. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of doing handovers right at the patient's bedside?

options.A: It prevents doctors from ever entering the patient's room
options.B: It completely removes the need for any written nursing notes
options.C: It reduces the total number of required vital sign checks
options.D: It allows patients to hear their care plan and ask questions

explanation: Bedside handovers make patients part of their own healing journey and help catch any mistakes early! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the main thing a nurse does when acting as a health advocate?

options.A: Diagnosing complex medical conditions independently
options.B: Prescribing emergency medications during shortages
options.C: Speaking up for patients and protecting their rights
options.D: Managing the financial budget of the health facility

explanation: You got this! Being a health advocate simply means standing up for your patients, defending their rights, and helping them navigate the healthcare system. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T7#GNS124_U4_T7_h1)

question: How do you place AED pads on a patient who has a pacemaker lump on their upper left chest?

options.A: Place the AED pad at least one inch away from the device
options.B: Refuse to use the AED because implanted devices block shocks entirely
options.C: Disable the pacemaker using a magnet before applying the pads
options.D: Place the AED pad directly over the bulge to improve shock delivery

explanation: Just place the pad about an inch away from the pacemaker bulge. If you put it right on top, it can absorb the shock energy and damage the implanted device. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h6)

question: You just gave an injection on a busy ward. What is your very next step with that used needle?

options.A: Recap the needle carefully and place it in the regular paper bin
options.B: Throw the syringe into the general black bin bag
options.C: Leave the syringe on the bedside table for the cleaning staff
options.D: Drop the uncovered needle directly into a rigid safety box

explanation: Never recap needles! Drop them straight into a puncture-proof safety box to protect yourself and others from accidental pokes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T17#GNS122_U3_T17_h4)

question: Why should a nurse focus on health problems that residents care about the most?

options.A: It saves the hospital from spending any money on medical supplies
options.B: Residents are more motivated to participate when the project matches their interests
options.C: Government regulations legally force citizens to attend health meetings
options.D: It guarantees that no one in the village will ever fall sick again

explanation: When people see you addressing a problem they actually care about, they will gladly join in and help! [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which group of psychiatric drugs is most famous for causing rapid weight gain?

options.A: Short-acting sleeping tablets
options.B: Standard over-the-counter vitamins
options.C: Mild herbal anxiety supplements
options.D: Second-generation antipsychotics

explanation: Correct! These medications heavily impact metabolism and appetite control, often leading to rapid weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: Why is a patient in the prodromal stage often a high risk for spreading germs to others?

options.A: Their immune system has completely stopped functioning
options.B: They feel well enough to move around while carrying germs
options.C: They shed the highest volume of toxic waste products
options.D: Pathogens multiply exclusively during this specific phase

explanation: Spot on! Because they don't feel super sick yet, they keep moving around and unknowingly expose people around them. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h6)
